articles.title: Allen exits NI Open with Brown loss on return
articles.summary: Mark Allen's return to action ends in defeat as he becomes the latest big name to exit the Northern Ireland Open, losing to Jordan Brown at the Waterfront Hall.
body: Allen, who had not played since his agonising World Championship semi-final loss to Wu Yize in early May, lost 4-2 to Brown in the all-Northern Ireland first-round contest in Belfast.
Former world number one Allen becomes the 10th top-16 player to fall at the first hurdle this year, with Ronnie O'Sullivan, Judd Trump and Mark Selby among the early casualties.
Allen, 40, took the opening frame on Tuesday afternoon but 39-year-old Brown hit back by taking the next two.
While Allen levelled the match at 2-2, Brown built breaks of 53 and 80 in the final two frames to progress.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany to miss Bayern’s clash with Arsenal due to legs-affecting virus
articles.summary: Kompany told to rest after struggling with infection. His assistant poised to oversee Champions League game. Vincent Kompany is touch and go to be in the Bayern Munich dugout against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday night as he battles a debilitating virus that has affected his legs.
body: Kompany has been told to rest after he struggled through Bayern’s 6-1 home win over RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday, after which the club’s sporting director, Max Eberl, addressed the media instead of him. There have been reports in Germany that Kompany needed to lie down on his sofa at home after the Leipzig game and that the viral infection had affected an existing hip problem which meant he could hardly walk.

“It has affected his legs at times,” Danks confirmed. “He’s felt some pain in his legs. I’m not sure about the reports about him lying down on the couch. I think we can all have a lie down on the couch after a game. It’s just a virus. The doctors and experts know way more than I do. The most important thing we have encouraged is that he rests; he takes the time he needs – however long that may be.

“Unfortunately, I can’t give you any more – whether that’s tomorrow or whether that’s two or three days’ time. I don’t know. We just take it day-by-day and see how he is. Getting Vince to rest is a challenge. You know him as a person. He’s a real leader. He works hard.”

articles.title: US under-17 women beat Samoa 17-0 for biggest win in World Cup history
articles.summary: Result is largest margin at any age level of a World Cup. DiMaria is first to score six at Fifa finals since Haaland. Tournament is in year two of expanded 24-team field.
body: The United States began their U-17 Women’s World Cup campaign on Monday with a record-setting 17-0 win over Samoa the biggest win at any age level in World Cup history.

The result surpassed the previous record for margin at an 11-a-side World Cup, a 16-0 win by Morocco against New Caledonia in the 2025 U-17 men’s World Cup. Ten players scored for the US, and forward Maddie DiMaria led with six goals in Salé, Morocco.
“I wasn’t aware [we were breaking a record], but I’m super proud of this group and it’s nice that they have something like that behind their name,” US coach Ciara Crinion told Fifa’s website.

DiMaria, a 17-year-old high-schooler from St Louis who is committed to play in college at North Carolina, scored her first goal 63 minutes into the match. It was the most goals by a US player ever in any match and the most by any player in a Women’s World Cup match at any level.

articles.title: Why O'Sullivan faces battle to stay in world's top 16
articles.summary: Snooker's World Championship without Ronnie O'Sullivan is hard to conceive, after years of him being so often the central figure at the Crucible. But it may not be far away.
body: The prospect seems almost unthinkable, with the 50-year-old a near ever present in the top 16 of the world rankings since he became a professional in 1992.
However, the seven-time winner at the Crucible now faces a battle to maintain his place within the 16-man group guaranteed automatic entry to the World Championship.

Already down at number 13 in the world rankings, O'Sullivan fell in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open on Monday and is in need of prize money that would solidify his place among the current world elite.
Still seeking the eighth world title that would mean he surpasses former rival Stephen Hendry, O'Sullivan has said he would prefer to retire rather than ever enter qualifying events.

articles.title: Ronaldo let Manchester United down - Ten Hag
articles.summary: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag says Cristiano Ronaldo "let the team and let me down" during the Dutchman's spell at Old Trafford.
body: Portugal forward Ronaldo was in his second spell at United when Ten Hag took charge in the summer of 2022 but left in controversial circumstances a few months later.
"He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him," Ten Hag told The Athletic, external.
"I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United.
"Obviously, he's one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in."

articles.title: What is the longest a team has gone without winning a league game at home?
articles.summary: Burnley are on the brink of unwanted football history, should they fail to beat Portsmouth later this month.
body: Burnley will set an unwanted English football record if they fail to beat Portsmouth in their next home match on Saturday, 31 October.
The Clarets have not won a home league match since beating Leeds United 2-0 in the Premier League on 18 October, 2025.
Sheffield Wednesday currently hold the record for the longest time a team in England's top four divisions have gone without winning a home league match.
The Owls failed to win a league game at home for 376 days between April 2025 and May 2026.

body: Chet Holmgren’s blunt 5-word deflection on Victor Wembanyama making rivalry ‘personal’ appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

According to a Sports Illustrated feature by Chris Mannix, Holmgren was bullish on leaning into the rivalry and talked about his matchup with Victor Wembanyama, adding that he learned a lot from the Spurs’ 7-game win over the Thunder in May. Holmgren said he took away lessons from the 28 other teams in the league and didn’t relish the matchup. He also directed the question of whether the two have a rivalry to Wembanyama.

“You can’t get so wrapped up in just that, that you forget the process and the steps that it takes to work towards the goal we’re trying to work towards,” Holmgren told Chris Mannix about facing Wembanyama. “They’re a very talented young team. There’s no denying that. And I’d say, I mean, we’re a very talented young team too, and that leads to some very fiery, competitive basketball games.”

While many believe Wembanyama has embraced the rivalry on the court, he’s also downplayed it in media comments, including an interview with Taylor Rooks on NBA’s Prime Video coverage in December 2025.

articles.title: England crumble to defeat versus Pakistan in ODI tri-series opener
articles.summary: England crumbled to an 87-run defeat in their ODI tri-series opener against Pakistan in Rawalpindi as the batting severely malfunctioned after an excellent start.
body: England, who have won their last three bilateral ODI series, were cruising on 91-0 inside 15 overs in a chase of 303, only to end up being bowled out for 215 in 38.4 as home spinner Arafat Minhas backed up his maiden ODI half-century with figures of 6-40.

Visiting captain Harry Brook (5) was bowled by a beauty from Arafat after openers Ben Duckett (47) and Tom Banton (47) failed to build on a rollicking opening stand against a Pakistan side who rallied from 81-4 earlier in the day having being put in to bat.

The tourists then wilted once the hosts snapped a patient stand of 31 from 57 balls between Joe Root (33) and Sam Curran (27) from 128-3 with Arafat on a hat-trick once he removed Will Jacks (19) and Adil Rashid (1) from successive deliveries in the 39th over before he ran out Gus Atkinson (7) two balls later to clinch victory.
Arafat snared each of the final five wickets, including Jamie Overton (1), who holed out at long-on in what commentator Stuart Broad described as "an appalling dismissal", and Cox lbw for 18.

articles.title: NFL in Paris 'all systems go' despite riots in France
articles.summary: The NFL says it is "all systems go" as it prepares to make its historic debut in Paris on Sunday amid ongoing riots around the French capital.
body: New Orleans Saints will serve as the designated home team when they honour their French ties against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the nation's first regular-season game at Stade de France, live on Sky Sports NFL from 1pm.
It comes after civil unrest broke out across Paris over the weekend as peaceful protests were overshadowed by masked activists and vandals turning to violence and looting.
Brett Gosper, the NFL's head of Europe and Asia-Pacific, said the league is prioritising the safety of fans and the two travelling teams, but envisions no disruption to the game.
"It hasn't impacted it, but obviously we're keeping a good eye on that and we're in very constant daily contact with the French authorities on it," Gosper told Sky Sports.

articles.title: More star names at The Hundred in 2027 as overseas player quota grows
articles.summary: The player retention window for The Hundred 2027 tournament is now open, with the eight men's and women's teams allowed to make signings or retain players from their 2026 squads.
body: Before the direct signing window from January 20 - February 3, and the auction - set for March but the date yet to confirmed - teams can first look to secure their favourite players from 2026.

Also, in a change to squad sizes for 2027, teams can now carry a maximum of 19 players (and minimum of 16), with the number of overseas players allowed rising from four to five - and from three to four in playing XIs.
The window opened on October 19, 2026 and closes on January 15, 2027. Teams can announce retained players from their 2026 squads at any point during this period.
Each men's and women's squad can retain up to 16 players. Retained players will stay on their 2026 salaries for the 2027 season.
